All processor methods used are documented: create_full_parser, create_fragment, next_tag, is_tag_closer, set_bookmark, has_bookmark, seek, add_class, get_updated_html, release_bookmark. Main adherence loss: this is flat tag/class mutation, where the docs recommend WP_HTML_Tag_Processor; create_full_parser-first is also not the documented fragment-friendly choice.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all 18 trial-case executions passed, and there were no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs succeeded because the Tag Processor overview clearly assigns flat, position-based class edits to WP_HTML_Tag_Processor; next_tag documents case-insensitive real-tag matching and excludes comments/raw text/incomplete tokens; add_class documents appending to existing classes; get_updated_html is documented as the right output method after queued edits; and the set_bookmark docs explicitly describe re-setting one name as the idiom for remembering the last matching tag. Near-miss: trial-1 chose WP_HTML_Processor and create_full_parser first. The docs do warn that create_fragment is usually more appropriate for chunks and that the lighter Tag Processor suffices for flat class edits, but a model can still over-read 'document or fragment' as a reason to use the structured processor. That did not fail the frozen cases, but it is less robust: if WP_HTML_Processor aborts on unsupported markup before a later H2, a bookmark-based scan may be incomplete unless get_last_error is checked or the Tag Processor is used instead.

doc_gaps.problem: A mixed contract like 'document or fragment' can lead readers to try create_full_parser first even when the operation is only a flat tag/class edit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a decision note: for byte-preserving tag, attribute, or class edits, use WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for both complete documents and fragments; choose create_full_parser only when full-document structural parsing, HEAD/doctype handling, or normalized serialization is required.

doc_gaps.problem: The Processor bookmark section omits the Tag Processor's explicit statement that setting an existing bookmark name moves it, which is the key contract behind 'last occurrence' scans.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Mirror the Tag Processor wording that re-setting the same bookmark name moves the bookmark and is the supported idiom for remembering the last matching token, with the Processor-specific caveat that virtual tokens cannot be bookmarked.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md / HTML Support / next_tag() mutation patterns
doc_gaps.problem: The docs describe unsupported-markup aborts, but do not tie that risk directly to bookmark-driven mutations after a scan: 'last seen' may not mean 'last in the input' if the Processor stopped early.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add guidance that after an HTML Processor scan whose result drives an edit, callers should check get_last_error before seek/edit/output and fall back according to their contract; for flat mutations that should continue across unsupported structural markup, prefer WP_HTML_Tag_Processor.
